requirements.evidence: Contract is fully present: queues/tickets migrations with cascade FKs, unique (entity_id, slug)/(queue_id, code) and the composite index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_044442_create_queues_table.php:14-23, database/migrations/2026_10_29_044443_create_tickets_table.php:14-27); stale-safe lock + active check and 5-attempt retry (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:33-58); insertion-order/malformed-skipping nextCode (app/Models/Ticket.php:89-103); single-call check and AuthorizationException (app/Models/Ticket.php:113-131); factories incl. forQueue and explicit codes (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:24-40); Queue/Entity/Ticket relations and enums. Gaps are edge-case only: call() reads status from a possibly stale instance without a transaction/lock, and the write-once guard does not cover bulk updates.

conventions.evidence: Docs kept in sync as required: docs/business-rules.md:72-80, docs/database-schema.md:4 and :147-155, CHANGELOG.md:12; domain write lives in an invokable action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:34); both migrations have reversible down() (:30, :34); deliberate fillable on Ticket (app/Models/Ticket.php:17-26). Deviations: Queue declares fillable through the #[Fillable] attribute (app/Models/Queue.php:11) while Ticket and sibling models use $fillable, an API that needs verifying against the installed Laravel version; call() authorizes with an inline membership query (app/Models/Ticket.php:117-122) rather than a policy/gate, although the task's contract puts call() on the model.

security.evidence: Membership is checked server-side before any mutation and the outsider path leaves the ticket unchanged (app/Models/Ticket.php:117-124; tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:256-269); negative priority and inactive queue are rejected before persisting (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:29-49); no request input, rendering or secrets in this diff. Gap: Ticket's $fillable accepts every column including code, status and called_by_user_id (app/Models/Ticket.php:17-26), so a future controller passing request data to Ticket::create() could write/forge call fields.

tests.evidence: Broad Pest suite: migrations/columns/unique keys (tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:19, :37), entity/queue cascades (:54, :62), enums (:70), factories and sequential codes (:97, :107), explicit legacy code (:110), nextCode insertion order and >999 growth (:116, :127), no reuse after delete (:138), malformed codes (:147), issuance defaults (:159), stale inactive queue (:177), collision retry (:187), negative priority (:213), write-once (:220), call exactly once (:228), non-waiting (:243), outsider unchanged (:256). Missing/weak: labels_i18n and the DB-level defaults are never asserted (factory sets is_active/status/channel explicitly, :619-621, :683-694) and the test named '...and suggested index' (:37) never asserts the index.

simplicity.evidence: One lean invokable action, no service/repository layer, no speculative abstraction (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php); code allocation reuses a model creating hook instead of duplicating logic in the factory (app/Models/Ticket.php:67-71). Nits: unreachable trailing throw (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:68) and two overlapping unique-violation branches (:55-63, :71-78); nextCode plucks every code of the queue on each issuance (:93-95).

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names and useful PHPDoc (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:36-49, app/Models/Ticket.php:84-111, :113-120); consistent with sibling factories (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:9-25); no dead debug code or leftover comments beyond explanatory ones (app/Models/Ticket.php:48-51, :66-70).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: enums, exception, models, action, factories, migrations, docs, changelog and one test file; no unrelated refactors or extra features (call-next selection, UI and totem API are left out, matching 'Out of scope'). The event listener in tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php:187-197 exists only to simulate a code collision.

issues.explanation: Queue opts into mass assignment through `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable` while Ticket and the sibling models use `$fillable`; verify the attribute exists in the installed Laravel version (otherwise it is silently ignored and QueueFactory creation throws MassAssignmentException) and prefer the project's `$fillable` style.

call() checks `$this->status` on the in-memory instance and saves without a lock or transaction, so two concurrent callers (or one holding a stale instance) can both pass the `waiting` check and the second overwrites `called_at`/`called_by_user_id`, weakening 'exactly once'.

Ticket's `$fillable` includes `code`, `status`, `called_by_user_id` and `issued_at`, so any future `Ticket::create($request->all())` would let a client mass-assign write-once and call fields; narrowing fillable to issuance-only fields would keep the write-once invariant at the mass-assignment boundary too.

The write-once guard relies on model events, so `Ticket::query()->where(...)->update([...])` bypasses it and can change `code`/`priority`; the task's wording ('any Eloquent save/update') arguably includes that path.

Unique violations are handled twice — a specific `UniqueConstraintViolationException` branch plus a generic `QueryException` branch with message sniffing — and the final `throw new RuntimeException` at :68 is unreachable; one branch plus a comment would be leaner.

The test titled '...and suggested index' only asserts columns and code uniqueness, never the `(queue_id, status, priority, issued_at)` index; likewise `labels_i18n` casting and the DB-level `is_active`/`status`/`channel` defaults are untested because the factory sets them explicitly.

review.summary: Adds the queue/ticket domain core end to end: migrations, models and relations, enums, `InactiveQueueException`, an invokable `IssueTicket` with row locking and unique-code retries, factories, synced docs/CHANGELOG and a thorough Pest suite. The requirements and the tricky display-code/issuance edge cases are implemented correctly; deductions come from an unverified and inconsistent `#[Fillable]` attribute on Queue, a non-atomic single-call guard, overly broad Ticket `$fillable`, and a few test details that are claimed but not asserted.
